title: llame instance configuration
description: Operator-owned instance configuration for llame (config-as-code, openspec/changes/instance-config + providers-and-models-as-code). Optional; a setting absent from this file takes its documented built-in default (there is no bare environment-variable fallback — the environment reaches settings only via {env:...} tokens written in this file). String values may contain {env:NAME}, {env:NAME:-default}, {path:LOCATION}, and {path:LOCATION|json:POINTER} interpolation tokens (RFC 6901; POINTER must select a JSON string), resolved once at boot, except models[].systemPromptFile, which is always a literal host path handled by the dedicated prompt loader. This document is both the editor-facing schema (referenced via the top-level $schema key) and the boot-time validator — the same artifact, so they cannot drift.

interpolationToken.description: A whole-value interpolation token: {env:NAME}, {env:NAME:-default}, {path:LOCATION}, or {path:LOCATION|json:POINTER} (RFC 6901; POINTER must select a JSON string). Only legal on non-string settings as the ENTIRE value (no surrounding text) — string settings may embed tokens anywhere instead.

numberOrToken.description: A positive integer, or a whole-value interpolation token that resolves to one.

nullableNumberOrToken.description: A positive integer, null, or a whole-value interpolation token that resolves to one of those.

nullableString.description: A plain string, or null to explicitly unset (overriding any legacy environment fallback). May embed {env:...}/{path:...} tokens anywhere in the string.

heartbeatSecondsOrToken.description: The job-queue's native worker-liveness window: a positive integer >= 10 (pg-boss's own floor for queue heartbeatSeconds), or a whole-value interpolation token that resolves to one.

providerType.description: Executable provider client implementation. Only "openai" is supported in this slice (native OpenAI + any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, e.g. Ollama). Anthropic is a follow-up: this enum is strict-closed so a config naming an unimplemented type fails validation, not execution.

providerEntry.description: A single provider connection. Providers are duplicable — two entries of the same `type` with distinct `id`s (and typically distinct `baseUrl`s) coexist, e.g. hosted OpenAI alongside a local Ollama.

id.description: Operator-chosen identifier, unique within `providers[]`. Referenced by `models[].provider`.

key.description: Provider credential. Absent, null, or a resolved-empty `{env:...}` token means keyless (e.g. a local Ollama with no auth) — the client is constructed without raising a missing-credential error.

baseUrl.description: Provider endpoint base URL. Absent/null uses the client implementation's own default (OpenAI's hosted API for `type: "openai"`).

mcpServerEntry.description: One operator-managed MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint. Header values may use the standard single-pass interpolation syntax and remain private server configuration.

type.description: Aliases for MCP Streamable HTTP. Use "stdio" for a local child-process server; deprecated HTTP+SSE is not supported.

url.description: Absolute http(s) MCP endpoint without username/password userinfo. May use {env:...}/{path:...} interpolation.

headers.description: Optional static request headers. Names and values must be non-empty; values may use {env:...}/{path:...} interpolation.

mcpStdioServerEntry.description: One operator-managed local MCP server, run as a child process and spoken to over stdin/stdout. The child executes on the llame host as the llame user with llame's filesystem and network access and is not sandboxed: configuring one is a trust decision equivalent to installing software on that host.

command.description: Executable to run, resolved against the child's search path or given as a host path. Never shell-interpreted. May use {env:...}/{path:...} interpolation.

args.description: Ordered arguments. There is no field accepting a whole command line as one shell-interpreted string. Each element may use {env:...}/{path:...} interpolation.

env.description: Environment for the child, merged over the MCP SDK's small base allowlist (HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, TERM, USER on POSIX). llame passes nothing else of its own, so a credential llame holds does not reach the child unless named here. Values may use {env:...}/{path:...} interpolation.

cwd.description: Working directory for the child. Absent means it inherits llame's, which is deployment-dependent — set it if the server resolves relative paths.

embeddingDistanceMetric.description: Distance metric the model's vectors are compared under. Only "cosine" is supported in this change — closed on purpose so a config naming an unimplemented metric fails validation, not execution.

embeddingModelEntry.description: A single declared embedding model (chat-search-embeddings). Reuses an existing providers[] connection rather than introducing a parallel credential or endpoint concept.

id.description: Stable internal key. Application code and stored vectors reference this — NEVER the provider-side model id. Referenced by a corpus's `search.*.embeddingModelId` selection.

provider.description: References a `providers[].id`. An id not defined there fails boot naming this embedding model and the dangling reference.

providerModelId.description: The server-only model id sent to the provider. Never derived from `id`, never returned to a client.

dimensions.description: Vector width this model produces. Every returned vector is validated against this before it is persisted.

batchSize.description: Documents per provider request. A throughput knob only — excluded from the binding-ledger comparison, so tuning it never conflicts with vectors already stored under this key. Defaults to 32.

revision.description: Optional model revision/version tag, recorded in the binding ledger alongside providerModelId.

documentPrefix.description: Optional text prepended to document content before embedding (asymmetric document/query models, e.g. E5/BGE's "passage:" convention).

queryPrefix.description: Optional text prepended to a search query before embedding — the query-side counterpart to documentPrefix.

modelPricing.description: Per-million-token USD pricing. Display/telemetry metadata only — never affects executability.

modelReasoning.description: Declares that this model accepts a reasoning-effort request parameter, and which values it accepts. Presence IS the declaration — there is no separate availability flag.

effortLevels.description: Opaque provider-native effort tokens (bare string) or { value, label } objects, in the operator-authored order clients present them in. Uniqueness is on value only (enforced at boot, not via uniqueItems). Deliberately unconstrained beyond nonblank value: provider vocabularies differ and change between releases. Values are identifiers; label is optional display metadata.

defaultEffort.description: The level value used when a request omits `effort`. Required whenever this object is present — no default is implied from list position. A value absent from effortLevels[].value fails boot naming this model.

cacheInvalidatedByEffortChange.description: Whether CHANGING effort between turns invalidates this model's provider-side prompt cache. Operator-declared because the behavior is model-specific and partly undocumented; nothing in the provider, model id, or level list predicts it. Published so a client can warn before an owner pays for a full prefix re-read. Default false.

modelEntry.description: A single executable model catalog entry. It independently resolves one complete system prompt: the packaged project default when systemPromptFile is omitted, or the configured whole-file replacement when present.

id.description: Opaque llame model id, e.g. "system:openai:gpt-5.4-mini". Clients treat this as opaque; it is never parsed for routing.

provider.description: References a `providers[].id`. An id not defined there fails boot naming this model and the dangling reference.

providerModelId.description: The server-only model id sent to the provider. Never derived from `id`.

contextWindowTokens.description: Required, execution-critical: sizes the context-compaction trigger (x COMPACTION_WINDOW_RATIO) unless `compactionThresholdTokens` overrides it.

compactionThresholdTokens.description: Optional explicit compaction trigger threshold for this model, overriding the `contextWindowTokens x COMPACTION_WINDOW_RATIO` default. Internal execution config — not returned by `GET /api/v1/models`.

systemPromptFile.description: Optional literal host path to this model's complete replacement system prompt. Relative paths resolve from the active llame.config.json directory; absolute paths remain absolute. This field does not support {env:...} or {path:...} secret interpolation. Prompt files are Handlebars templates. Renderable paths are exactly {{model.id}} and {{model.name}}; a leading backslash emits a literal expression. Conditionals ({{#if}} / {{#unless}}), comments, and whitespace control are supported. Rendering is single-pass and never re-evaluates its own output. Any other path, a helper, a partial, or unescaped {{{...}}} output fails startup naming the construct; a path with no value renders empty rather than failing. Missing, unreadable, non-file, empty, or invalid prompt content fails startup without falling back to the project default. Prompt contents are owner-visible; the host path is never returned by the public model catalog.

$schema.description: Reference to this published schema, for editor autocomplete/hover. Ignored by the loader — the sole exemption from the closed schema below.

defaults.description: Instance-level model pointers. Deliberately not under the `models` key, which holds the executable catalog itself. Each pointer, when set, must reference a `models[].id` or startup fails.

modelId.description: Default model id used for new chats when the user hasn't chosen one. Must reference an entry in `models[]` when set (boot failure otherwise); unset means model selection fails as a server configuration error at request time.

titleGenerationModelId.description: Model id used to generate chat titles. Must reference an entry in `models[]` when set (boot failure otherwise); unset means title generation is skipped.

providers.description: Provider connections (providers-and-models-as-code, #167). Supersedes the OPENAI_API_KEY / OPENAI_BASE_URL bare environment variables — those names remain valid {env:...} interpolation inputs for an entry's key/baseUrl.

models.description: The executable model catalog (providers-and-models-as-code, #167), superseding the formerly hardcoded server catalog. Each entry's `provider` must reference a `providers[].id`.

embeddingModels.description: Declared embedding models (chat-search-embeddings). Optional; an instance declaring none is unchanged from today and schedules no embedding work.

search.description: Per-corpus search settings (chat-search-embeddings). Selection is expressed per corpus, never as one instance-wide flag, so corpora embedding at different rates cannot strand one another.

embeddingModelId.description: Must reference an entry in `embeddingModels[]` when set (boot failure otherwise). Unset (default) means the chat corpus has no intended model and produces no embedding work.

mcpServers.description: Operator-managed MCP Streamable HTTP servers in portable .mcp.json named-object form. Absent means no remote servers.

knowledge.description: Optional operator-managed root for private Knowledge Space directories. The loader validates only the interpolated absolute-path shape; it never probes the filesystem.

root.description: Absolute process-local root beneath which trusted code allocates stable Knowledge Space ID directories. May contain {env:...}/{path:...} interpolation and is never public or caller-selectable.

runs.description: Durable run execution timers and limits (#48/#50; liveness collapsed onto the job-queue's native heartbeat, durable-run-workers D7). No compaction.* or context-window setting exists here — compaction is model-driven, never an instance knob.

maxOutputTokens.description: Output-token reserve used when admitting a request against the model context window. It does not yet cap provider output; enforcing that cap remains part of the run-budget feature (#91). File-only (no legacy env var).

heartbeatSeconds.description: The job-queue's native worker-liveness window, in seconds: while a run's job is in flight the worker auto-signals liveness at half this interval, and the queue's monitor fails+retries the job if the signal lapses this long — worker-death detection, not an application heartbeat. Falls back to RUN_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS, then 15.

timeoutSeconds.description: In-process wall-clock budget, in seconds: while its worker is alive, a run exceeding this is aborted in-process and recorded as a terminal run.expired (distinct from a user run.cancelled). Falls back to RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, then 300.

trustProxy.description: Express trust-proxy setting: a non-negative integer hop count, 'true'/'false', or a subnet spec. Falls back to TRUST_PROXY, then unset (no proxy trusted — client IPs are taken at face value).

poolSize.description: Per-process postgres pool `max`. A run holds a connection per runAs transaction, so set this >= the process's total run concurrency (sum of the active worker profile's group concurrencies) plus HTTP headroom; poolSize x replicas must stay within Postgres max_connections. Falls back to DB_POOL_SIZE, then 10.

tools.description: Tool-calling loop availability (openspec/changes/tool-calling-loop). The operator allowlist is the entire availability story this slice — no policy engine exists yet (D3).

allowed.description: Tool permissions admitted for advertisement/execution. Default: empty array (no tools advertised or executable — fail closed). Code-owned ids must exist in the registry. Exact canonical mcp-tool-id-v1 ids and the single namespace form mcp__<configured-server>__* may name a configured mcpServers entry without requiring successful discovery at boot; the wildcard is a case-sensitive literal id-prefix permission and remains only in restart-applied configuration.

maxStepsPerRun.description: Hard cap on tool-requesting steps per run before the loop stops offering tools and drives the model to answer from accumulated context. Falls back to the built-in default, 20.

callTimeoutSeconds.description: Global timeout, in seconds, for a single tool call (a tool may declare a per-tool override at registration — a code-level property, not a config key). Falls back to the built-in default, 120.

workers.description: Worker profiles (durable-run-workers D2/D4): profile name -> the fixed consumer groups it consumes and each one's main-queue concurrency, selected at boot by LLAME_WORKER_PROFILE (default 'all'). A profile referencing an unknown group name fails boot. Built-in 'all' (every group at concurrency 1) and 'web' (no groups) are always available; an entry here replaces that profile name wholesale.

additionalProperties.description: One worker profile: consumer-group name -> main-queue concurrency (positive integer).
